newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico overnight Cetes rate ends sharply down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico overnight Cetes rate ends sharply down.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 100 basis points at 21.00 percent on Monday amid expectations that primary rates would fall later in the day, traders said.
"Paper was most in demand toward the close. Basically it was fueled by expectations that auction rates would fall, and by some nationalized corporations stepping in to buy," a dealer said.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 35 basis points at 22.65 percent.
Banco de Mexico brought forward its weekly auction of government securities, scheduling the sale for Monday, because Constitution Day on Wednesday will cut the working week short.
Auction results are due out at 2030 EST/0130 GMT.

A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed an average predicted assignment rate of 21.62 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury certificates), which would represent a decline of 29 basis points from the auction rate last week.

Traders said predictions of falling primary rates were bolstered by a drop in U.S. long-bond yields and expectations that the Federal Open Market Committee would not change U.S. interest rate policy during its meeting Tuesday and Wednesday.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds fell to 6.74 percent, from 6.81 percent in early trade.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 385 million pesos to offset a slight liquidity shortfall through one credit auction, which it assigned overnight at 22.33 percent.

Total maturities estimated for Tuesday were estimated at a relatively light 385 million pesos, but traders noted liquidty would come under additional pressure from a demand for cash ahead of the public holiday on Wednesday.
